title: Morphological Study of ZnO Particles Crystalline Faces for Photocatalytic Degradation of Rhodamine B
content: X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) and high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) are fundamental techniques to characterize materials' elemental composition and morphology at the nanoscale. It has been shown that the synthesis method technique influences the morphology of ZnO. In particular, hydrothermal and solvothermal synthesis produce significant differences in the crystallinity, size, and shape of the nanoparticles, directly affecting their photocatalytic performance. The motivation of this work is to evaluate how these morphological variations of ZnO impact the photocatalytic degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) under direct sunlight. The study was conducted through EDS and HAADF-STEM to correlate ZnO elemental composition and morphology with photocatalytic activity.
